objective.text: Account for skipped per-model events when using a mass update query.

difficulty.rationale: Recognize the lifecycle difference when replacing individual saves with one query.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: An updated observer writes a per-record audit entry. A refactor replaces a loop of model saves with Record::where("name", "old")->update(["name" => "new"]). The database changes, but audit entries disappear. What explains the regression?

options.text: The update is deferred until the matched models are read again.
options.rationale: The SQL update executes immediately; lazy hydration is not delaying the write.
options.misconception: The SQL update executes immediately; lazy hydration is not delaying the write.

options.text: Observers run only when an update also changes the primary key.
options.rationale: Ordinary instance updates dispatch events without changing their primary key.
options.misconception: Ordinary instance updates dispatch events without changing their primary key.

options.text: The observer runs once but receives a collection rather than a model.
options.rationale: Eloquent does not substitute a collection event for each updated model in this operation.
options.misconception: Eloquent does not substitute a collection event for each updated model in this operation.

options.text: The mass update does not hydrate each model, so per-model updated events are not dispatched.
options.rationale: The query writes rows directly; an observer requiring each model lifecycle is not invoked for each matched row.

explanation.summary: The query writes rows directly; an observer requiring each model lifecycle is not invoked for each matched row.
